punchline: Gibson says a child can have shelter, food and clothing and still carry a loneliness it cannot name.
thirty_sec: Lindsay Gibson writes about adult children of emotionally immature parents. From outside, life looked fine: the parents provided a home, food and clothes. Yet many of these children grow up with deep loneliness, disconnected relationships and low self-worth. Some retreat into a dream world of a better future, which can leave them with unrealistic hopes as adults.
